newsitem.title: UK: Labour seeks more Railtrack accountability.
newsitem.headline: Labour seeks more Railtrack accountability.

text.p: The UK opposition Labour Party said on Tuesday it wanted to make privatised rail infrastructure firm Railtrack Plc more accountable and criticised the company for falling behind on its investment commitments.

Labour's shadow transport secretary Andrew Smith said in a keynote speech to an Industry Forum conference on transport: "As a natural monopoly whose performance is critical for the whole system, Railtrack must be held to account for the quality and effectiveness as well as the financial value of its investment programme and for its property disposals. The first call on those should be for investment."
He described Railtrack's lack of investment as "wholly unacceptable."
Concerning freight, Labour said it planned to consult the industry on getting more traffic onto rail and off the road. As part of this drive it would propose a code of practice for Railtrack.

Labour said the code -- to be enforced by the rail regulator -- would require Railtrack to provide information and introduce procedures for dealing with new freight business requests and a general obligation to develop freight.
This is part of a wider policy to improve road management and develop rail usage further by passengers and freight.

Also on rail, Labour's Smith said that if elected, "We will review the existing arrangements for the achievement of network benefits which fragmentation of the network puts at risk." This includes through-ticketing and better information on fares. Labour said it was prepared to consider certain measures regarding licence conditions to achieve this.
It will consider beefing up the rail regulator's powers and make it more accountable to the government.
